title: The auth gate is a dead end on every gated intent
evidence: live: opened /contact, clicked any category → sheet with only "Continue" and "Continue with Google"; Escape does not close it, backdrop click does not close it. Same sheet on /properties/kame-home/form.
what: an anonymous visitor who expresses intent (contact us, book a stay, book parking) is shown a sign-in sheet with no close control, no "continue as guest", and no way back except the browser Back button. The sheet has exactly two buttons, both of which require an account.
why: this is every conversion path at its highest-intent moment. It also contradicts the home page, which says "No account needed." A visitor without an account cannot contact support or start a booking.
fix: add a visible close, an explicit "Continue as guest" where the task allows it, and set `aria-modal` plus a body-scroll lock; if sign-in is genuinely required, state the reason and the alternative (email) inside the sheet.
acceptance: Escape, the close button and the backdrop all dismiss the sheet; a guest can reach the booking form and the contact form without an account, or is told why not.

title: The payment step never shows what the stay costs
evidence: `step-05-payment.jpg` and `.json`
what: The breakdown is three lines: "Downpayment / 2 nights stay ₱2,000.00 / Total due now ₱2,000.00". There is no nightly rate, no stay total, no balance due on arrival, and the ₱10 voucher applied on step 2 does not appear. The listing says ₱4,500/night, so a 2-night stay is ₱9,000 and the guest cannot reconcile any of it.
why: This is the money screen. A guest is asked to transfer funds to a phone number with no way to verify the amount, and cannot tell whether ₱2,000 is a deposit, a discount, or the whole stay.
fix: Show the full ladder: nightly rate x nights, fees, voucher, total stay, downpayment due now, balance due at check-in. Carry the voucher through from step 2. Round consistently.
acceptance: Step 5 shows at least rate, nights, subtotal, voucher, total, due now, balance; the numbers reconcile with the listing price and the calendar selection.

title: Invalid invite link is a total dead end
evidence: `./screenshots/public/auth__accept-invite__m390.jpg`, `auth__accept-invite__d1440.jpg`; live: `probe-p4b.json → acceptInvite` (`links: []`, body text `"Kame | Space"`)
what: The page renders a bare grey canvas with one centred card reading "This invitation link is invalid." There is no logo, no header, no footer, no navigation, and the DOM contains **zero** links or buttons. A host who clicks an expired or already-used invite from their email has nothing to do next.
why: This is the first impression for a brand-new invited teammate. The most common real cause (expired link) is also the most recoverable, and the page offers no recovery. It also silently breaks the invite flow's last step.
fix: Keep the error card but add brand chrome (logo, `--public-nav-h` header) and two actions: "Ask for a new invite" (mailto or support link) and "Sign in" (`/for-hosts/login`). Distinguish expired vs malformed vs already-accepted copy, since those need different next steps.
acceptance: `/accept-invite` with no token and with a bogus token both render the logo, one plain-language reason, and at least one working navigation control; keyboard focus lands on the card.

title: "On this device" is a build/cache debug panel on a guest page
element: bottom card — Version / Local build / Check updates / Offline / 144 KB used / Keep data / Clear saved data
evidence: `account__profile__m390.jpg`, `account__profile__d1440.jpg`
what: A card exposes "Version: **Local build**", "Offline 144 KB used", "Check updates", "Keep data", "Clear saved data". "Local build" is a developer string. "Keep data" and "Clear saved data" do not say *which* data (cached pages? drafts? the booking form you were filling?).
why: Guests are being shown implementation state and given a destructive-sounding button with no object. "Clear saved data" next to a PWA cache is one tap from losing an offline booking draft, and nothing says so. This is exactly the internal-tool leak the pass was asked to flag.

acceptance: No build, byte-count or cache jargon remains; any destructive control names what it deletes.

title: Guest Help is an empty shell with no search

title: `/onboarding` and `/verification-rejected` both redirect to the org Dashboard
evidence: `admin-gap__onboarding__d1440.jpg` and `admin-gap__verification-rejected__d1440.jpg` are pixel-identical to the org Dashboard; live `probe-p4b.json` — both land on `http://localhost:5173/org/kame-homes/dashboard` with `h1: "Dashboard"`

The onboarding entry point has no onboarding content, and the verification-rejected state has no UI at all: a host whose verification was rejected sees a normal dashboard, with a "Verification" item that looks half-selected in the sidebar and no explanation anywhere.
why: Verification is the gate on payouts and public pages. A host who fails it is silently dropped into a dashboard where nothing says they are blocked or why, and every payouts action will fail later with no context. Onboarding is the first-run experience for every new host.

title: Result grids do not fill the viewport, so one result floats in an empty page
evidence: `shots/listings__properties__d1440.jpg` (260px card, ~1000px empty), `shots/listings__parkings__d1440.jpg`, `shots/listings__developments__d1440.jpg`, `shots/listings__properties__m390.jpg` (card ~155px wide, title truncated "Condo in San…"), `live3.json` (`cardW: [260]`, `mainW: 1440`)

title: Calendar renders 27 contrast failures and does not distinguish available, blocked and past
evidence: `shots/guest-flow__calendar__d1440.jpg` (days 1 to 17 nearly invisible, 23/24/28/29/30 faint mint), `manifest.json` `calendar` `contrastCount: 27-28`, `calendar-cells.json` (1 to 18 `disabled: true`, 19 to 22 open, 23/24 closed, 25 to 27 open, 28 to 30 closed)
what: Past days, blocked days and today all render in variants of near-white. Only open days are legible. There is no legend, no "unavailable" label, and the current day (18) is a pale mint block that looks like a blocked day. Nothing communicates which days are clickable.
why: Picking a date is the first action in the funnel, and it depends on spotting a 1.1:1 difference. Users will assume the calendar is disabled or broken.
fix: Three explicit states at AA contrast: open (ink on white, hover/focus ring), blocked (struck or hatched with "Unavailable" tooltip), past (muted but legible). Add a one-line legend. Give today a ring, not a fill.
acceptance: All day numbers pass 4.5:1 against their cell; a legend explains open/blocked/past; blocked cells expose `aria-disabled` plus an accessible "Unavailable" name.

title: At 320 the calendar is clipped and its own CTA covers the last week

title: The trip page is unopenable for the guest it was emailed to

Check the link or sign in with the email you booked with."), `live2.json` `trips` (the account's own 5 trips do not include this booking)

element: Header badge, summary card, step header

what: (a) A white circle at the top of the card is meant to hold an image but renders the listing title, which overflows the circle in every direction ("zure Monaco - Level 2 - Slot 27" clipped at both widths). title: A future trip is filed under PAST
evidence: `account__trips__m390.jpg`, `account__trips__d1440.jpg`; live `probe-p4b-3.json → tripRows` = `Monaco 2604Feb 1-2, 2027Completed`
what: With today at 18 Nov 2026, "Monaco 2604 · Feb 1–2, 2027 · Completed" sits in the PAST group, above an Oct 24–26, 2026 trip that is labelled "Ready for check-in".
why: The grouping is by status, not date, so the list contradicts itself: a completed stay in the future and an unfinished stay in the past. A guest scrolling for their next trip finds it below the fold under a heading that says the opposite.
fix: Group by date (upcoming = check-in ≥ today), and show status as a badge only. Separately, flag the Oct 2026 booking that is still "Ready for check-in" as stale.
acceptance: No trip with a future check-in date appears under PAST; group membership is derivable from the visible date.

title: Broken thumbnail on the parking trip row
evidence: `account__trips__m390.jpg` (broken-image glyph); live `probe-p4b-3.json → tripImgs` — `es.unsplash.com/photo-1590674899484-...` returns `naturalWidth: 0`
what: The parking booking's thumbnail is a broken image (the host is `es.unsplash.com`, a malformed variant of `images.unsplash.com`). The other rows fall back to a suitcase icon.
why: A broken-image icon on the guest's own trip list is the single most "unfinished" signal in the account area, and it appears on every viewport.
fix: Fix the stored URL, and add an `onError` fallback to the same suitcase icon the other rows use so a bad URL can never render a broken glyph.
acceptance: No `naturalWidth === 0` images on `/account/trips`; a deliberately bad URL falls back to the icon.

title: Same parking listing named two different ways
evidence: `admin-gap__onboarding__d1440.jpg` shows "Azure Monoco – Level 2 - Slot 27"; `account__trips__d1440.jpg` and live `tripRows` show "Azure Monaco - Level 2 - Slot 27"
what: One listing renders as **Monoco** with an en dash and a hyphen in the host surface, and **Monaco** with two hyphens in the guest surface.
why: It is the same bookable object. A guest searching their email for "Monoco" will not find "Monaco", and the dash mix makes the string look machine-assembled.
fix: Store one canonical display name; build it as `Development · Level 2 · Slot 27` from parts rather than a free-text string.
acceptance: The listing name is byte-identical across guest trips, host bookings and emails.

title: Messages is one row over 600px of nothing, authored by "seed-owner"
evidence: `account__messages__m390.jpg`; live `probe-p4b-3.json → msgs` (main text is one row; tall box 652px, `scrollH 955`)
what: The card holds a single conversation row ("Monaco 2604 / **seed-owner** / about 3 hours ago / AUDIT-MESSAGE please ignore") and then ~600px of empty white. At 390 there is no thread pane and no empty-state copy for it. The sender is rendered as the raw account handle `seed-owner`.
why: Two problems in one viewport. The layout is a two-pane desktop pattern collapsed without a plan for the collapsed state, and a guest is shown an internal account handle instead of a person or property name.
fix: Collapse to a single list with real sender names ("Kame Space · Monaco 2604"), and either open a thread route or show a "Select a conversation" empty state instead of blank card. Never render the auth handle.
acceptance: At 390 the list fills the card or shows an explicit empty state; no message shows an email local-part as the sender.

title: Vouchers have no expiry, no code, and no way to use them
evidence: `account__vouchers__m390.jpg`; live `probe-p4b.json → vouchers` (no toast on tapping the code, button list contains no per-voucher action), `probe-p4b-3.json → vouchers1440`
what: One card: "READY TO USE / STAY10 / ₱10 off / Monaco 2604 · Awarded 10 days ago / Book again". There is no expiry, no minimum spend, no copy-code control (tapping the code does nothing), and no Used/Expired section. "₱10 off" is 0.2% of a ₱4,500 stay.
why: A voucher you cannot copy, whose validity you cannot check, and whose value is negligible is decoration. The guest has no path from "I have a voucher" to "it applied".
fix: Show code with a copy button and a copied state, expiry date, and the condition. Add Used/Expired groups. Give the seeded voucher a realistic value.
acceptance: Copying a code produces a visible confirmation and a pasteable value; each voucher states an expiry date.

title: Favorites truncates the only listing at 390
evidence: `account__favorites__m390.jpg`; live `probe-p4b-3.json → fav` — card 156px inside a 324px `grid-cols-2` parent, title renders "CONDO in San…"
what: The grid is `grid-cols-2` below `sm`, so each card is 156px wide and the title truncates to "CONDO in San…". With one favourite, the right half of the row is empty.
why: The card's title is the only way to tell what was saved, and it is cut. On a saved-items page the identifier must never be the thing that truncates.
fix: One column below `sm` (or 2 columns only from 400px), two-line clamp for the title instead of single-line ellipsis, and keep the price/rating row intact.
acceptance: At 390 the full listing title is readable and the card fills its row.

title: New ticket sheet opens with the Details field sliced by Submit
evidence: `account__tickets-new__m390.jpg`, `shots/live-ticket-390.png`; live `probe-p4b.json → ticketNew` (dialog 704px tall at y=140, textarea at y=794, Submit at y=788)
what: On first open, the sheet's scroll region ends behind the sticky Submit bar: the "Details *" label is half visible and the textarea sits under the footer. Scrolling reaches it (textarea moves to y=437 once scrolled), so it is recoverable, but the first frame shows a form that looks clipped.
why: A required field that appears cut in half at the exact moment the user is deciding whether to fill the form is a drop-off point, and it looks like a layout bug.
fix: Add bottom padding to the scroll region equal to the footer height, or start the sheet at full height (`h-[100dvh]`) with the options block scrollable.
acceptance: At 390×844 the last field's label is fully visible or fully out of view on first paint; nothing is sliced by the footer.

title: Playbook renders the database slug under every article title
evidence: `admin-gap__admin-playbook__d1440.jpg` — `audit-blocked-dates`, `extend-your-calendar`, `collect-outstanding-balances`, `highlight-amenities-in-title`, `publish-public-page-updates`
what: Under each human title, the raw key renders in monospace-ish muted text, at the same visual level as the body copy.
why: This is a content tool for super admins; the key is useful for developers, not for the person deciding whether a tip should be published. It reads as an un-stripped internal field.
fix: Move the key to a tooltip or the edit dialog, or render it as a `code` chip visually subordinated to the description. Never make it the second line of the card.
acceptance: Card subtitle is human copy; the key is only visible on hover/expand or inside edit.

title: The bare "31" pill is a pagination size with no pagination
evidence: live `probe-p4b-2.json → playbookCtl` = `{tag: BUTTON, role: combobox, txt: "31", aria "Items per page", w: 56}`; 17 playbook articles and 31 FAQs on one page
what: A small pill showing only "31" floats at the right of the list. Its accessible name is "Items per page". There is no page indicator, no prev/next, and both lists fit on one page, so the control changes nothing visible.
why: An unlabelled number in the corner of a list is a puzzle, and a page-size selector with one page is a dead control that implies missing content ("there are more, but where?").
fix: Remove it while total ≤ page size; when it is needed, label it on screen ("Show 31") and pair it with real paging.
acceptance: The control is absent when the list fits on one page; when present it is labelled and changes the visible rows.

title: Playbook clamps body copy to two lines on mobile with no way to expand
evidence: `admin-gap__admin-playbook__m390.jpg`; live `probe-p4b-3.json → playbookClamp` = `webkitLineClamp: "2", scrollHeight 114, clientHeight 46`
what: The description is clamped to 2 lines and ends mid-sentence ("Review your calendar each…"). There is no expand affordance and the card is not tappable except for the toggle and the pencil/trash.
why: The advice is the entire value of the item. Super admins are being asked to publish or delete tips they can only half read.
fix: Remove the clamp (the cards already scroll), or add a "Show more" toggle and make the whole card expand.
acceptance: Every article's full text is reachable at 390 without editing it.

title: 31 FAQs, nine categories, no search and no filter
evidence: `admin-gap__admin-faqs__d1440.jpg` (stat cards: Total 31, Published 31, Unpublished 0, Categories 9); live `probe-p4b.json → faqs` = `inputs: []`, `combobox: []`
what: The page has no input of any kind. Categories are headings only. To find one FAQ among 31 in 9 groups the user scrolls a 5,000px list.
why: This is the tool for answering "what do we tell hosts about X", and the only affordance is scrolling. It is also the page where a wrong or stale answer would be fixed.
fix: Add a search field over question + answer, a category filter, and a Published/Unpublished filter derived from the existing stat cards.
acceptance: Typing a phrase narrows the list to matching FAQs; choosing a category narrows to that group.

title: Ops reports show "CRITICAL 0" in red on every row and two different "current weeks"
evidence: `admin-gap__admin-ops-report__d1440.jpg`, `..._m390.jpg`; live manifest contrast sample (HIGH 0 at 3.6:1 ×3)
what: Every row carries four pills. "CRITICAL 0" is red on all four rows, including the three healthy ones, so the loudest colour on the page means zero. Row labels mix conventions: "Current week · Nov 16–23", "Week of · Nov 11–18", "Current week · Nov 15–18" (two rows both claim "Current week" with different ranges). Timestamps have no timezone.
why: Severity colour is an alarm channel. Painting a zero red trains the reader to ignore red. The three labeling conventions and the two overlapping "current weeks" make the list unusable as a history.
fix: Hide zero-count pills; show only CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM when > 0. Standardise the label to "Week of <Mon DD>" plus an explicit "manual run" tag, and add "Asia/Manila" to timestamps.
acceptance: No zero-value pill renders; no two rows share a "current week" label with different ranges.

title: Ops report detail exposes "Copy agent prompt" and env-var names
evidence: live `probe-p4b-4.json → opsDetail` = `Copy agent prompt | Download .md | Send email | ... SKIPPED Sentry errors | Not configured (SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_ORG_SLUG, SENTRY_PROJECT_SLUG)`
what: The report header offers "Copy agent prompt" as a top-level action, and source status explains itself by naming unset environment variables.
why: "Copy agent prompt" reveals the internal AI ops workflow inside a product admin surface and is meaningless to anyone who does not already know the pipeline. Env-var names are a developer's debugging shortcut, not a status message.
fix: Move "Copy agent prompt" behind a developer menu or remove it from the product surface. Rewrite source rows as "Sentry: not connected" with a "Connect" link.
acceptance: The report page has no reference to an agent prompt or to an env-var name; every skipped source states the user-level consequence.

title: The AI page shows a projection below actual spend and a chart with no bars
element: KPI row and "Cost by feature" chart
evidence: `admin-gap__admin-ai-usage__d1440.jpg`
what: "Spend $1.13" beside "Projected this month **$1**" (a projection lower than spend to date, and formatted without cents). "Cost by feature" renders an empty plot: axis $0.00–$4.00, no bars, with the single series label "Dashboard assistant (complex turn)" floating in the middle of the plot area. "Feature health" reports Calls 0, Credits 0, Errors 2 (100%).
why: Spend is money. A projection below actual and a 100% error rate on zero calls means at least one number is wrong, and an admin cannot tell which. The empty chart reads as a rendering failure.
fix: Format all currency to 2dp with one formatter; make projection `max(spend, forecast)` or hide it until mid-period; render the empty chart as a real empty state ("No AI spend in this range"); guard the error percentage against a zero denominator.
acceptance: Currency formatting is identical across the tile row, the chart renders bars or an empty state, and no percentage is computed from zero calls.

title: Payment rail switches lose their row at 390
evidence: `admin-gap__admin-payment-settings__m390.jpg` — "QR Ph" with the switch on the next line, left-aligned
what: Below `sm` the label and its switch stack vertically, so the control sits under the text at the left edge instead of opposite it. Each rail consumes two lines.
why: The pattern breaks the platform's own settings-row convention and makes a three-item list look like six rows. A left-aligned switch also loses the "this row is on" reading.
fix: Keep label left / switch right on one row at every width (`justify-between`, `shrink-0` on the switch), with the description wrapping under the label only.
acceptance: At 390 each rail is one row with the switch at the right edge.

title: Development detail truncates a section name and drops the section nav on mobile
evidence: `admin-gap__admin-development__d1440.jpg` ("Document Requirem…" with no tooltip); `admin-gap__admin-development__m390.jpg` (no rail at all)
what: At desktop the rail truncates "Document Requirements" with no `title`/tooltip. At 390 the rail disappears, leaving a page of 12 stacked sections with no in-page navigation, so reaching "Danger Zone" means scrolling the entire form.
why: The rail is the only map of a long form. Truncated at one size and missing at another, the map is unavailable exactly where the page is longest relative to the viewport.
fix: Widen the rail or allow two-line labels; on mobile replace it with a sticky section chip row (or a select) that jumps to sections.
acceptance: No section label is truncated without a tooltip; at 390 all 12 sections are reachable within two taps.

title: 15 unnamed controls and up to 89 sub-44px targets on the development page
evidence: manifest `admin-development` — `unnamedControls: 15`, `smallCount: 89` (1440) / `65` (390); `admin-gap__admin-development__d1440.jpg` (three ~28px circular buttons over the cover photo)
what: The image action buttons are ~28–32px and carry no accessible name; the same overlay repeats on every photo tile.
why: On touch these are hard to hit, and a screen reader announces 15 anonymous buttons in the middle of a media form.
fix: Use `MobileHeroActionButton`-style invisible hit pads (44×44) and `aria-label`s ("Set as cover", "Replace photo", "Delete photo") that include the photo position.
acceptance: `unnamedControls` is 0 on this route and every tile control measures ≥44×44 including its pad.

title: Property sidebar cuts a nav item mid-word at 900px
evidence: `admin-gap__prop-tickets__d1440.jpg`, `admin-gap__prop-docs__d1440.jpg`, `admin-gap__public-page-edit__d1440.jpg` — "Public Pages" sliced horizontally behind the plan card; live `probe-p4b-2.json → sidebar1024` = nav `scrollHeight 810` / `clientHeight 613`, `overflow: auto`
what: The nav scrolls, but the last visible row is clipped by the pinned plan card with no fade, so it looks like a rendering bug rather than a scroll region.
why: Team/Settings/Help & Support sit at the bottom of this list. A cut label reads as broken chrome and hides that there is more.
fix: Add bottom padding to the scroll region plus a white-to-transparent fade above the plan card, and scroll the active item into view on mount.
acceptance: No nav label is ever visually sliced; the fade indicates scrollability.

title: Announcements use a red "error" dot for informational items
evidence: `admin-gap__prop-announcement__d1440.jpg`
what: Every item (payout reminder, Meta reconnect, a maintenance window, a pool cleaning notice) carries a red dot and a coloured left rail. The KPI row offers four overlapping categories: Active 4, Action required 1, Attention 1, Updates 2. "Read all" appears twice, once per section. The payout item's body says "Open Finance if you see a banner."
why: Red is the platform's destructive/error colour. Using it for unread makes a routine pool-closing notice look like an incident, and "Active vs Attention vs Action required" cannot be decoded without an explanation. "If you see a banner" asks the user to go looking.
fix: Unread = a neutral or primary dot; reserve red/amber for the severity the item actually has. Reduce the KPI row to Unread / Action required / All, or label them as filters. Rewrite the banner sentence as a direct instruction.
acceptance: Informational announcements use no destructive colour; the KPI labels are mutually exclusive and act as filters.

title: Team KPI roles sum to more members than exist
evidence: `admin-gap__org-team__d1440.jpg`; live `probe-p4b-3.json → teamKpi` = `Total Members 5 | Full Access 1 | Operations 5 | Read Only 0`
what: 1 + 5 + 0 = 6 against a total of 5, while the member list shows 1 Full Access and 4 Operations. Whatever the extra Operations member is (paused? invited?), the row contradicts itself.
why: These tiles are the summary an owner reads before changing seats or upgrading. Numbers that do not add up make every other tile suspect.
fix: Derive the role tiles from the same query as the list and include paused/invited members explicitly (or exclude them consistently), so the sum equals the total.
acceptance: The three role tiles plus pending invites reconcile to Total Members.

title: Team tabs become three 36×32 unlabelled-looking icons at 390
evidence: `admin-gap__org-team__m390.jpg`; live `probe-p4b-3.json → teamTabs` = three tabs `36×32`, label text visually hidden, accessible name present
what: Below `lg` the tab labels collapse to icons only: a people icon, an envelope, a shield. The selected state is not visually distinguishable, and the targets are 36×32.
why: Accessible names survive for screen readers, but a sighted user on a phone gets three cryptic glyphs and no current-tab indicator, on the page that controls who can see what. The 36×32 size is also under the 44px touch minimum.
fix: Keep short labels ("Members", "Invites", "Roles") at 390 in a segmented control, or move to a bottom-sheet picker; enforce ≥44×44 hit area and a clear selected pill.
acceptance: At 390 each tab shows text or an explicit selected state, and every target is ≥44×44.

title: A notification's title and body name different guests
evidence: `admin-gap__parking-notifications__d1440.jpg` — title "Rafa Mercado", body "June Vale requested 3 nights at Monaco 2604."
what: The row header is one guest's name; the description attributes the request to another.
why: In a notification list the bold line is what the user acts on. Mismatched identity makes it impossible to know whose request is pending.
fix: Bind the title to the same subject as the body (the requesting guest), and put the stay dates in the metadata line.
acceptance: Title and body of every row reference the same guest.

title: Four rose-coloured KPI tiles make notifications look like an outage
element: Unread / Messages / Telegram on / Connected tiles
evidence: `admin-gap__parking-notifications__d1440.jpg` (rose icon chips on all four, all values 0 or 0/3)
what: All four tiles use a rose/pink chip and icon, including "Unread 0" and "Messages 0". The pink family is the platform's destructive tint.
why: The page's first impression is an alarm, with zeros in every tile. Two of the four ("Telegram on 0/3", "Connected 0/3") do not say what the denominator is.
fix: Use neutral or primary chips for counts; reserve rose for a genuine failure (a failed send). Relabel as "Telegram alerts · 0 of 3 modules on" and "Connected channels · 0 of 3".
acceptance: No zero-value tile uses a destructive tint; both `x/3` tiles name their denominator.

title: "Manage" degrades to a share-looking icon at 390
evidence: `admin-gap__parking-notifications__m390.jpg` (single circular arrow icon in the green hero, no label) vs `..._d1440.jpg` ("Manage" button)
what: The page's only settings entry point becomes an icon that reads as "share" or "export", with no label at mobile widths.
why: The most important action on the page becomes guesswork, and the icon is not the conventional gear that would at least hint at settings.
fix: Use the standard settings gear with an `aria-label`, or keep the word "Manage" at 390 (space exists in the hero).
acceptance: The mobile action is a gear or a labelled button, with an accessible name.

title: Telegram tab reads like a spec document
evidence: live `probe-p4b-4.json → parkTelegram` — `Telegram delivery | Turn every Telegram alert on or off at once. Your module settings stay saved. | Nothing sent yet | Sent alerts from the last 15 days show up here. | Connect a module in Manage | Delivery must stay on | Failed sends show a Failed badge`
what: The panel ends with three sentence fragments that describe how the system behaves ("Delivery must stay on", "Failed sends show a Failed badge") rather than a state or an action.
why: Copy that documents the UI inside the UI is the clearest internal-tool tell in this pass. A host cannot act on "delivery must stay on".
fix: Replace with states: an empty state ("No alerts sent yet · Connect a module"), a disabled-state hint on the toggle when delivery is off, and a legend only if a "Failed" badge is actually on screen.
acceptance: No helper line describes implementation rules; every line is a state or an action.

title: The editor renders three `<h1>`s, two of them "Showcase"
evidence: manifest `prop-public-page-edit d1440` `h1: ["Showcase","Monaco 2604","Monaco 2604",...]`; live `probe-p4b-2.json → editor390.h1` = `["Showcase","Showcase","Monaco 2604"]`
what: Two visible "Showcase" headings and the preview's own `h1` all render as `<h1>`, and the desktop count reaches seven.
why: Heading order is the primary navigation for screen readers; seven `h1`s across an editor and its preview is unusable, and the duplicate "Showcase" is also visually redundant.
fix: One `h1` "Edit showcase"; demote the in-page editor title to `h2`; render the preview inside a container that scopes its headings (`role="presentation"` on the wrapper's outline, or heading levels offset via props).
acceptance: The route exposes exactly one `h1` and a monotonic heading order.

title: The global nav and footer change shape per page
evidence: consistency probe (`./screenshots/public/data/consistency.json`): 10 distinct nav link orders and 4 distinct footer link sets across 27 routes. On listing pages the header also renders breadcrumbs (`Home > Stays > Azure North Residences > Monaco 2604`) as nav links; on account pages the 8-tile account strip is appended to the same nav.
what: the primary navigation's contents and order depend on the page you are on, so the header cannot be learned. Account pages end up with two navigations because the tile strip is rendered inside `nav`.
why: navigation consistency is the cheapest wayfinding signal; here the second and third items move between pages.
fix: one header nav for the marketing shell (Developments, Properties, Parkings, Services) and a separate breadcrumb element outside `<nav>`; move the account strip out of the navigation landmark.
acceptance: the same 4 primary links appear in the same order on every marketing route; breadcrumbs and account tiles are not inside `<nav>`.

title: A Gmail address is the public contact address
evidence: footer `mailto:kameworks.tech@gmail.com` on 20+ routes; `/support` prints it twice; `/about` "Based in Manila … email kameworks.tech@gmail.com".
what: the product's only public contact is a personal Gmail account, repeated in the footer, the about page and the support page.
why: it reads as an unfinished side project, it is not on the product domain, and it gives no routing or record of guest issues.
fix: `support@kamespace.com` (or the domain's real mailbox) in the footer and contact page, with the Gmail retired.
acceptance: no `@gmail.com` address renders on any public page.

title: The public pricing page carries three competing recommendation badges
evidence: copy inventory: Starter "Best value", Pro "Most popular", Business "Recommended".
what: every paid plan claims to be the plan to pick. The carousel also opens on Business, so the first plan a visitor sees is the most expensive one with a "Recommended" badge.
why: three recommendations cancel out, and the badge stops being a decision aid.
fix: one badge on one plan, chosen deliberately (usually the middle tier), and open the carousel on Free.
acceptance: exactly one plan carries a badge; the first card shown is Free.

title: The Free plan advertises "Finance management", which is a paid capability
evidence: copy inventory lists "Finance management" and "Maintenance reminders" under Free; the measured tier matrix (report 19) shows `financeReporting` and `maintenanceReporting` gated to Starter, and export is gated with `upgradeHook`.
what: the plan card promises a capability the product gates. A host on Free can open Finance but cannot export or report.
why: plan copy that overstates the free tier produces refund requests and support tickets.
fix: rename to what Free actually gets ("View bookings and expenses") or move the line to Starter, and make the card match `plans-feature-matrix.md`.
acceptance: every bullet on every plan card maps to a feature key and tier in the matrix.

title: "Reviews" in the host nav points at a section that does not exist
evidence: live: `document.getElementById('reviews')` is null on `/for-hosts`; clicking the link leaves `scrollY` at 0 and the URL hash unchanged.
what: the nav item does nothing. `#features` and `#how-it-works` work.
why: a dead nav item is the first thing a skeptical host clicks.
fix: point it at the reviews section (add an id) or remove the item until the section exists.
acceptance: clicking Reviews scrolls to a reviews section.

title: /services is a "Coming Soon" stub in the primary nav, with a date filter on it
evidence: screenshot `marketing__services__d1440.jpg`: "SERVICES / Coming Soon" with seven chips, a search bar with "What / Search services" and "When / Add dates", and ~40% empty space above and below.
what: a nav item that promises a capability leads to a placeholder; the search bar offers a date range for a service that has no dates; the chips look interactive.
why: it spends a primary nav slot on nothing and invites clicks that go nowhere.
fix: remove Services from the nav until it ships, or make it a "notify me" page; drop the date field on service search.
acceptance: no primary nav item leads to a placeholder page.

title: "Developer controls" is rendered on the guest payment step, and it is the root cause of LG-02
element: Card between "Payment terms" and the cancellation policy
evidence: `./screenshots/public/live/step-05-payment.jpg`, `step-05-payment.json` (text: "Developer controls / Control which actions run upon form submission. / Save data to database / Save image assets to Supabase Storage / Send email / Paste Booking Info from Clipboard / Generate New Data")
what: The payment step of a public booking form renders an internal panel with three submission toggles and two debug buttons, including "Generate New Data: Populate form with random sample data", which is what fills the form with fake identities.
why: A guest is asked for a GCash receipt directly above a control that can silently disable "Save data to database", "Save image assets" or "Send email" for their submission. This is both a data-loss risk and the most unprofessional thing on the product.
fix: Gate the whole panel behind an explicit dev/demo flag (never `import.meta.env.DEV` in a shipped build path that local prod data uses) or behind super-admin, and remove "Generate New Data" from the guest render entirely.
acceptance: Submit path in a normal session contains no element matching "Developer controls", "Generate New Data" or "Paste Booking Info"; submission toggles default to on and are not exposed.
verifiedNote: Dev builds only (`!import.meta.env.PROD`). Not shipped to production, but it can silently disable the database write and the email on any local or unbuilt run.

title: Public host page publishes the seed identity and seed copy
element: Host header, host card, review attribution
evidence: `shots/listings__host-public__d1440.jpg`, `shots/listings__host-public__m390.jpg`, `copy.json` (`seed-owner`, `Local demo host for the canonical seed dataset.`)
what: The hero reads "Kame Space" with "Hosted by seed-owner" and the bio line "Local demo host for the canonical seed dataset." `seed-owner` is the operator account name; the bio is build tooling language.
why: A guest-facing profile that says "canonical seed dataset" reads as a test environment. It also exposes the internal account naming convention.
fix: Seed a real host display name and a human bio, or hide the "Hosted by" line when the host record is the platform account. Never surface account emails/usernames on public pages.
acceptance: `/hosts/kame-homes` contains no `seed-`, `demo`, `dataset`, `example.com`, or internal account identifiers.
verifiedNote: Seed data rather than product logic: the seeded org publishes `seed-owner`, a demo bio and `manager.demo@example.com`. Needs a seed guard, not a redesign.

title: Nine routes have no h1
evidence: `manifest.json` `h1: []` for each of those ids at 390/768/1024/1440
what: The page title is an `h2` ("Check Availability", "Guest Advise Form", "Guest Review", "Pay to confirm") or missing entirely (listings start at "Homes in San Fernando" as an h2).
why: Screen-reader navigation and search-result structure lose the page identity; the browser tab and the page heading disagree.
fix: Promote the primary page title to `h1` on each route and keep section headings below it.
acceptance: Every listed route returns exactly one `h1` matching its purpose.

title: Sort has no price option
evidence: `live-sort.mjs` -> options `Recommended, Highest Rated, Most Reviews, Newest`
what: The only sort options are recommendation, rating, review count and recency. Price is filterable but not sortable.
why: On a ₱400 to ₱4,500 inventory, price order is the most common intent, and its absence pushes users into the price filter.
fix: Add "Price: low to high" and "Price: high to low".
acceptance: Sort list includes both price orders and reorders the grid accordingly.

title: Filter defaults flip between sibling listing pages, and parking search drops "Who"
element: Filter rail default state, search bar fields
evidence: `shots/listings__properties__d1440.jpg` ("Hide Filters", open), `shots/listings__parkings__d1440.jpg` ("Show Filters", closed), `shots/listings__development-properties__d1440.jpg` ("Show Filters"), `copy.json` parkings search has only Where/When
what: Properties opens with filters expanded; parkings and the development sub-pages open collapsed. The parking search bar has two segments; property and development have three ("Who 2 guests").
why: The three listing types look like three different products, and "2 guests" for parking would be meaningless anyway, so the asymmetry needs a rule rather than an accident.
fix: Pick one default (collapsed everywhere) and one search bar composition, hiding "Who" only where the entity has no guest concept, consistently.
acceptance: All listing pages share the same filter default and search field set, with documented exceptions.

title: The parking search bar pins itself over the site navigation on scroll
evidence: `shots` live `live-parkings-scrolled.jpg` (nav links hidden behind the pill), `live3.json` (`bar top: 17, height: 46`, class `fixed left-0 top-[-3px] z-[55]`; header `0-81, z-50`)
what: After any scroll, the search pill fixes to the top of the viewport at a higher z-index than the header, covering Developments / Properties / Parkings / Services. Its labels also change from "Where / Search parkings / When / Add dates" to "Parkings / Anytime".
why: Scrolling makes global navigation unreachable, and the collapsed labels stop describing an action.
fix: Pin the search bar below the header (respect `--public-nav-h`) or collapse it into the header as a single button. Keep the same labels in both states.
acceptance: On scroll at 1440 all four nav links remain visible and clickable; the search control does not overlap the header.

title: The developments list renders a condo listing priced at ₱0 per night
evidence: `shots/listings__developments__d1440.jpg`, `__m390.jpg`, `copy.json` ("1 development", "Condo in San Fernando", "₱0", "/ night", "1 home")
what: The single development result is titled like a property ("Condo in San Fernando", with a "Condo" type badge), and its price line reads "₱0 / night · 1 home". A development is not nightly-priced.
why: A zero price is the most damaging string on a travel site, and the card does not describe a development at all, so the page's whole premise is unclear.
fix: Development cards should show name, developer, city, "1 home · 1 parking" and a real "from" price computed from available units, or omit the price entirely.
acceptance: No ₱0 anywhere; development card is titled with the development name and shows inventory, not a nightly rate.

title: Development detail spends its hero on a 135px strip and explains nothing
element: Hero, overlapping identity card, page body
evidence: `shots/listings__development-detail__d1440.jpg`, `shots/listings__development-detail__m390.jpg`
what: The hero photo is a letterboxed band with the identity card overlapping its lower half. The type appears twice (badge "Condominium" and icon row "Condominium"). Beneath it: four amenity chips and two one-item carousels. There is no description, address, map, developer detail, or availability context.
why: The page is the landing surface for a building, and a guest learns nothing about living there beyond "has a gym".
fix: Taller hero (min 320px at 1440), remove the duplicated type, add an About block, address + map, developer, and make the two carousels one "Available now" section with inventory counts.
acceptance: The page answers what the development is, where it is, who built it and what is available above the fold and in the first two screens.

title: At 320 the bottom tab bar covers the development's primary CTA
evidence: `live5.json` `devCta` (`View Homes` top 625, bottom 669; nav top 643 -> `covered: true`), `shots/listings__development-detail__s320.jpg`
what: On first load the fixed bottom nav overlaps the lower half of the "View Homes" button, so the primary action is partly unclickable.
why: The 320px class of phones is small but real, and the overlapping target is the page's main conversion.
fix: Add bottom padding to the page equal to the tab bar height and/or reduce the hero card height so both CTAs sit above it.
acceptance: At 320 no interactive element intersects the tab bar on first load.

title: "Submit review & continue" looks enabled but is disabled, and the fixed nav covers the first rating rows
evidence: `shots/guest-flow__guest-review__m390.jpg` (pale green submit above Not now), manifest `guest-review` `stickyCovered: 5` at 390 and 768, `live3.json` `reviewCovered` (Check-in row 655-734 against nav top 693, `main` padding-bottom `0px`)
what: The disabled submit renders in brand teal at ~60% opacity, which reads as an active primary button; clicking does nothing and nothing says a star rating is required. On first load the fixed nav sits over the Check-in and Communication star rows.
why: A guest writes a review, taps submit, and gets silence. The star rows they need to complete are partly hidden behind the nav at the same time.
fix: Use an unmistakable disabled style plus a helper line ("Add a star rating to continue"), and add bottom padding so no form row sits under the nav.
acceptance: The disabled state is visually distinct, explains the missing input, and no rating row intersects the nav at 390 on load.

title: The form's own copy is internal jargon
element: Title, email helper, guest blocks, reminder
evidence: `step-01-guest.json`, `shots/guest-flow__form-signed-in__m390.jpg`
what: "Guest Advise Form" (what is being advised?), "Use an email you can access. Your GAF will be sent there for Azure North check-in." (GAF is never expanded), "Add more guest" (grammar), "Maximum Guests Reminder" followed by a 44-word run-on that mixes occupancy, the pool and age rules.
why: Guests must understand what they are submitting and where the document goes. Unexplained acronyms and run-ons produce support tickets.
fix: See the Copy rewrites table.
acceptance: No unexplained acronyms on the guest path; helper text under 20 words per line.

title: Form data entry is inconsistent and the desktop layout wastes the screen
element: Date fields, step rail, card width
evidence: `step-02-stay.json` ("11/25/2026" in inputs, "Nov 25, 2026" in the summary above it), `shots/guest-flow__form-signed-in__m390.jpg` (rail reduced to "Guest … 1/5"), live signed-in form `scrollHeight` 3,611-3,884 at 1440 with a single ~400px column
what: Dates render in two formats on one screen. On phone the five-step rail collapses to the current step name plus "1/5", so the guest cannot see that documents and payment are coming. At 1440 the entire form is one narrow column, producing a 3,600px scroll with half the viewport empty.
why: Guests abandon long forms when they cannot see how much is left, and desktop users scroll through a phone layout.
fix: Use one date format (a readable "Wed, 25 Nov 2026"). Keep a compact 5-dot rail with labels on mobile. At 1024+ use a two-column field grid with the step summary as a side rail.
acceptance: One date format per screen; mobile shows all five step labels; at 1440 the form is at most two screens tall for step 1.

title: The pets step contradicts its own policy and shows pet fields whether or not a pet is coming
element: Pet policy block and pet detail fields
evidence: `(live probe, not committed)` (Pets step text), `step-04-pets` run
what: The policy says "Only one toy/small dog is allowed" and then the prefill is Pet Type "Dog", Pet Breed "Persian Cat", age "6 months old", with a vaccination date and two required uploads. The detail fields are open and required while the "No pets on this stay" option is still selected above them.
why: A guest with a cat is told cats are not allowed by a field that accepts them, and a guest with no pet still faces required pet fields.
fix: Show pet details only when "Yes, I'm bringing a pet" is chosen, make the policy match what the form accepts (or restrict the type to dog), and clear any prefilled pet data.
acceptance: Selecting "No pets" hides and un-requires all pet fields; the accepted species matches the policy text.

title: Three different cancellation sentences, one of them ungrammatical
evidence: `copy.json` property-detail ("Moderate", "Full refund of what you paid up to 3 days before check-in.", "100% of paid at least 3 days before check-in."), `shots/listings__property-detail__m390.jpg` ("Free cancelation until you've paid up to 3 days before check-in."), `step-05-payment.jpg` ("Moderate / Full refund of what you paid up to 3 days before check-in. / Percentages apply to what you have paid. / 100% of paid until Nov 22, 2026")
what: The same policy is stated three ways across two screens, with "cancelation" (one l) on mobile and "cancellation" on desktop, and "until you've paid up to" is not parseable.
why: Refund terms are the most scrutinised copy on a booking. Ambiguity here becomes a dispute.
fix: One canonical sentence per policy with a date: "Free cancellation until 22 Nov 2026. After that, 100% of what you paid is non-refundable." Use it on the listing, the form and the receipt.
acceptance: Identical policy text and date on listing, form step 5 and confirmation; correct spelling.

title: One action, four names
route: /properties/kame-home (Reserve), /properties/kame-home/showcase (Request stay, Book now), home page (Send a request), parking (Reserve)
evidence: `copy.json` (`Reserve`, `Request stay`, `Book now`, `Send a request`), `shots/guest-flow__showcase__d1440.jpg`
what: The same next step is labelled four ways. Within the showcase page alone, the hero says "Request stay" and the footer CTA says "Book now".
why: Two labels for one action inside one page makes guests think they are different flows (request vs instant book), which is a real product distinction the labels should not fudge.
fix: Decide whether it is a request or an instant booking and use one verb everywhere ("Request to book" if a host confirms).
acceptance: One primary CTA label for the booking entry across listing, showcase and home.

title: The stay guide's document status contradicts itself and uses internal identities
element: Check-in documents row, host block, chapters
evidence: `shots/guest-flow__stay-guide__d1440.jpg`, `live2.json` `stayGuide` links and text ("Approved GAF", "PENDING", "viewer.demo", "manager.demo@example.com", "CHAPTER 01/02/03")
what: A row labelled "Approved GAF" carries the status "PENDING". The host block shows `viewer.demo` and the footer contact is `manager.demo@example.com`. Chapters open with "Welcome! Here's everything you need to know…", "Welcome to our property! Please follow these guidelines to ensure a pleasant stay:", "Thank you for staying with us! Please follow these steps for check-out:".
why: A guest looking for their check-in document sees "approved" and "pending" at once, and an email to `manager.demo@example.com` bounces. The template prose reads as filler on a page people rely on at arrival.
fix: Label the row by the document ("Azure North guest form") with one status chip. Show the real host display name and a working contact. Replace the welcome openers with the actual instruction.
acceptance: Status is unambiguous; no example.com or account usernames on the page; each chapter starts with the instruction, not a welcome.

title: The rating distribution bars render at equal length
evidence: `shots/listings__property-detail__s320.jpg`, `shots/listings__property-detail__m390.jpg` (all five bars visually the same width)
what: The histogram next to "4.5 / 10 reviews" draws five bars at effectively the same length, so it looks like every rating has equal share and contradicts the 4.5 average.
why: A broken chart next to a rating reads as fake reviews.
fix: Bind bar width to the actual counts and hide the block when there are no counts; otherwise replace it with the two category scores already shown.
acceptance: Bar widths are proportional to counts and sum to 10 for this listing.

title: Hero alt text describes a different image
evidence: live: evaluated `section img` on `/` → `alt="Sunlit living room in a Kame Space stay, looking out to the water"` with `src=/marketing/home/hero-day-1280.avif` (the resort image)
what: The alt text describes an interior living room. The rendered image is an exterior resort with towers and waterslides. The paired night image uses `alt=""`.
why: Screen-reader and low-vision users get a false description of the page's primary visual, and the mismatch is the kind of thing that erodes trust in every other alt string on the site.
fix: Write alt text that matches the replacement photograph (per MK-01), or mark the decorative layer `alt=""` if the H1 already carries the meaning.
acceptance: Alt text and rendered image describe the same subject; verified by reading the alt string against the screenshot.

title: Booking explainer burns 4.2 viewports for five short lines
evidence: live: section height 3,545px at both 390 and 1440 (≈4.2 viewports); `crops/home-dead-d1440.jpg`; `live-home-2350.png` shows one step on screen with the rest grey
what: The five-step story is driven by scroll position: each ~700px of scroll advances one step. Live it works (step 1 → 5 as you scroll), but the page holds ~4 screens for ~40 words of copy, and any full-page capture or fast scroll shows large empty grey bands. On mobile, the example-trip card keeps a fixed height sized for the richest step, leaving ~180px of blank white card under "Valid ID" (see `home-messages-390.png`).
why: It is the longest section on the homepage and delivers the least information per pixel. Users who scroll quickly see empty grey and assume the page is broken; users who scroll carefully spend four screens learning five facts.
fix: Cut the pinned height to ~1.5 viewports (one screen per two steps, or drive it with a normal in-flow stepper). Let the example card size to its content per step. Keep the 1→5 progress affordance.
acceptance: Section height ≤ 1.5 × viewport at 390 and 1440; no blank region larger than 120px inside the example card on any step.

title: White label over a photo with no scrim ("Century Properties")
element: Development card photo overlay, bottom-left label
evidence: manifest contrast entry `Century Properties ratio 1.0 need 4.5 size 12`; `search-lower.png`
what: The development name is white 12px text placed directly on the building photograph, outside the dark gradient that covers only the right/badge side.
why: At 12px this fails AA even with a good backdrop; measured at 1.0:1 it is effectively invisible against the bright sky band of that photo.
fix: Put the label on a solid or gradient pill (as the "1 homes available" badge does), or extend the image scrim to full width at the bottom.
acceptance: The label's computed contrast against its rendered backdrop is ≥ 4.5:1 on every listing photo.

title: Result counts are glued into the section headings, and two filter systems compete
evidence: manifest `headings: ["Properties1", "Developments1", "Parkings1"]`; live `h2` innerText `Properties1`; `search-default.png` shows a "Filter properties" bar with "3 results" plus a second "All 3 / Properties 1 / Developments 1 / Parkings 1" tab row
what: The count badge is inside the heading element, so assistive tech announces "Properties one". Separately, the page offers both a "Filter properties" control with a "3 results" counter and a type tab row with the same counts.
why: Two controls doing overlapping jobs make the page feel unconsidered, and a heading that reads "Properties1" is a genuine screen-reader defect.
fix: Mark the count `aria-hidden` (or move it outside the heading) and give the heading a clean accessible name. Collapse the two filters into one: the tab row for type, the button for attributes/dates.
acceptance: Heading accessible names are "Properties", "Developments", "Parkings"; only one mechanism changes the result type.

title: Mobile type-chip row is clipped by the floating filter button
element: Sticky type chips vs the icon-only filter button
evidence: `search-390.png` shows "All 3 | Properties 1 | Developme…" cut mid-word under the ⊞ button; live boxes: Properties 83–156px, Parkings 158–232px, filter button at ~338px
what: The chip row scrolls horizontally but has no right padding to clear the floating filter control, so the third chip is truncated by it. "Parkings" is only reachable by scrolling.
why: On the phone, the page's primary segmentation control is partly hidden and partly illegible, and the icon-only filter button loses its label so nothing explains what it does.
fix: Add right padding equal to the filter button width + gap (`pr-14`), and keep a short text label on the filter control or move it into the header row above the chips.
acceptance: All three chips plus the filter control fit or scroll clear of each other at 320 and 390; no chip is overlapped by a button.

title: Empty-state recovery offers "Search nearby" to someone who typed a place
evidence: `search-empty.png`; live URL `/search?where=Boracay%2C+Aklan&adults=2`
what: The empty state offers "Search nearby" (a geolocation action) and "Clear place". Neither helps a user who wants Boracay or who simply misspelled something, and no alternative inventory is shown.
why: This is the one screen every failed search lands on, and it sends the user back to the beginning with no information gained.
fix: Offer "See all stays" and 2–3 nearest available destinations with counts ("San Fernando, 1 stay"), and keep "Clear place". Drop "Search nearby" unless geolocation actually returns inventory.
acceptance: From a zero-result search, one click reaches a page with at least one bookable listing.

title: Product tour panels show clipped screenshots and truncated captions
evidence: `for-hosts__for-hosts__d1440.jpg` (dashboard mock inside the panel is cut at both edges with empty white KPI cards; chip row ends "Fin…"), `for-hosts__for-hosts__s320.jpg` caption reads "Everyt…" and "Bookin…", `host-login2.png` left panel sidebar clipped ("…board", "ngs", "ws")
what: The embedded product screenshot is a fixed-width image placed inside a narrower frame, so it is cropped on every edge; the caption and chapter strip are ellipsized mid-word at small widths.
why: This panel is the proof of the product. Cropped UI with empty cards reads as an unfinished demo, and truncated captions look like rendering errors.
fix: Render the mock at the panel's actual size (or use a responsive screenshot at 2×), crop deliberately to a meaningful region, and let captions wrap instead of truncating. Make the chapter strip scrollable with edge fade rather than hard-clipping.
acceptance: At 320 and 1440, no caption or chip is ellipsized mid-word, and the dashboard mock shows a complete frame with no cut-off panels.

title: "1 booking workflow" presented as a headline statistic
evidence: `for-hosts__for-hosts__d1440.jpg` and `..._s320.jpg` — "14 connected modules · 1 booking workflow · AI assisted review · 24/7 background automation"
what: Three of the four stats are impressive-scale (14, 24/7, AI); the second is "1", which reads as either a typo or a joke.
why: A stats strip exists to build confidence; one weak cell drags the other three down and invites the question of what "1" is even counting.
fix: Replace with a countable, meaningful figure (e.g. "6 stages, one path" or "0 spreadsheets") or drop the cell and use three stats.
acceptance: Every stat in the strip is either a quantity that reads as an achievement or removed.

title: Host pages use a completely different navigation system
evidence: `for-hosts__for-hosts__d1440.jpg` header = Features / How It Works / Reviews / Pricing / Explore / Sign In; `marketing__home__d1440.jpg` header = Developments / Properties / Parkings / Services / Become a host? / Sign In
what: Two unrelated top-level navs share one logo and one footer. The four guest nouns are replaced by four host nouns, and the primary CTA flips from "Become a host?" to "Explore".
why: A visitor who lands on `/for-hosts` from the footer or an ad has no stable way back to inventory, and "Explore" (a bare button) is less clear than the "Become a host?" pattern used everywhere else. Two nav systems means two sets of maintenance and two sets of defects (see MK-20).
fix: Keep the site nav consistent and make the host area a clearly scoped sub-nav (Features / How it works / Pricing) with the global nav above it, or at minimum keep the "Explore" affordance labelled and identical across both.
acceptance: The same global nav renders on every marketing route; host-specific links sit in a visually distinct secondary row.

title: Every paid plan carries a permanent "20% off"
element: Plan price blocks and compare-table headers
evidence: `for-hosts__for-hosts-pricing__d1440.jpg`, `pricing-initial.png`, copy inventory: ₱499→₱399, ₱999→₱799, ₱1,799→₱1,439, ₱4,999→₱3,999, each with a "20% off" pill
what: All four paid tiers show the identical 20% discount, with no end date, no strike-through rationale, and no qualifying condition.
why: A discount that always exists is not a discount; it trains visitors to ignore the badge and invites the assumption that the real price will rise to the struck-through number later. It also threatens price-transparency expectations for a paid SaaS.
fix: Either run a real, dated promotion (with an end date shown) or show one price with no strike-through. If the 20% is a launch offer, state the end date next to the badge.
acceptance: No plan shows a strike-through price without a stated expiry, or all plans show a single non-discounted price.

title: Four plans claim three different kinds of recommendation
evidence: `pricing-initial.png` — Starter "Best value", Pro "Most popular", Business "Recommended", Managed "Hands-off hosting"
what: Three badges compete to be the recommendation ("Best value", "Most popular", "Recommended"), plus a fourth badge that is really a description. The subtitles also change axis per card: Starter = automation, Pro = reach, Business = AI, Managed = hands-off.
why: When everything is recommended, nothing is. The visitor is asked to compare four unrelated value propositions with no ladder, which is the main reason multi-tier pricing pages fail.
fix: One recommendation badge ("Most popular" on a single tier). Rewrite each subtitle on the same axis (who it is for), e.g. "For one property, no automation", "For 2–3 units with automated emails", "For teams running several properties". Move "Hands-off hosting" into the Managed card body.
acceptance: Exactly one plan carries a recommendation badge; all five subtitles share one grammatical pattern and one comparison axis.

title: Plan card accents introduce purple and amber into a teal system
evidence: `pricing-initial.png` — Starter lightning in mint, Pro arrow in a lavender square, Business sparkle in purple, Managed heart in amber
what: Four unrelated hues appear only on this page, outside the site's teal token set (DESIGN.md explicitly rules out purple-indigo accents).
why: The pricing page is where a buyer compares value; four competing accent colours add visual noise to the one place that should be calm and legible, and they do not encode any information (they are not tied to tier rank).
fix: Use the teal/neutral token set for all plan icons, differentiating tiers by fill weight or badge rather than hue.
acceptance: No purple or amber icon on `/for-hosts/pricing`; all icon accents resolve to teal/neutral tokens.

title: 36-question FAQ has no search, no anchors, and expands to 5,903px
evidence: `marketing__support__d1440.jpg`; live: 0 search inputs, 0 `details`, 0 `#` anchor links, 0 `h3`; after clicking "Show all 36" the document height is 5,903px
what: Twelve answers render fully expanded; the rest are hidden behind one button that dumps 24 more paragraphs into a single column. There is no way to filter, jump to a topic, or link to an answer.
why: Support is the page a frustrated user reaches last. All-expanded prose with no search forces full-page scanning, and agents cannot link a user to a specific answer.
fix: Add a search field (client-side filter is enough), an audience switch (Guests / Hosts) as tabs, `id` per question for deep links, and collapse answers to `<details>`/accordion so the page opens short.
acceptance: Typing into a support search filters questions; every question has a shareable `#anchor`; the page is under ~1,200px before any interaction on mobile.

title: Public support page is mostly host-dashboard internals
evidence: `marketing__support__d1440.jpg`; copy inventory shows 4 guest questions vs ~12 host questions before "Show all 36", covering "Export report", "New booking", "Import beside New booking", "Pending Review", "GAF"
what: A guest landing on `/support` (the footer link a guest is most likely to use) sees a majority of answers about a dashboard they cannot access, written in internal vocabulary (GAF, Pending Review, SD refund).
why: Guests bounce because the page does not answer their question in their language; hosts get operational copy on a marketing page instead of in-product help. The two audiences dilute each other.
fix: Default to the Guests tab, put host answers behind the Hosts tab, and expand guest coverage (change a date, cancel, refund timing, parking, ID upload) to at least parity. Translate internal status names into plain language.
acceptance: Guests tab answers ≥ 8 questions, contains no internal status or document acronyms, and is the default view.

title: "Sign in with your explore account"
evidence: `marketing__contact__d1440.jpg` subtitle: "Pick what your message is about. Sign in with your explore account to open a ticket."
what: "Explore account" is not a product concept anywhere on the site. The account is a guest account (`/for-guests/login`); "Explore" is also the label of a bottom-nav tab, so the sentence points at two different things.
why: Jargon at the exact moment the user needs to know whether they have an account. It makes a simple step feel like a membership requirement.
fix: "Pick a topic. Sign in to track your ticket, or email us instead."
acceptance: No internal account-type naming appears in public copy.

title: Ticket modal clips content mid-word and disables Submit without saying why
evidence: `contact-broken.png` — the attachment drop zone is sliced through the label at the scroll fold; live: `button "Submit" [disabled]` with no validation message and no `aria-invalid` on the fields
what: The scrollable body ends mid-word with no fade or border to indicate more content, and the primary action is disabled until all required fields are filled, with no inline explanation or error text.
why: A disabled button with no reason is a dead end for users who cannot tell which field is missing; a body that cuts a label in half looks like a rendering fault rather than a scroll region.
fix: Show inline required-field errors on blur/attempt and keep Submit enabled (validating on press). Add a fade or top/bottom border on the scroll region so clipped content reads as scrollable.
acceptance: Pressing Submit with missing fields shows a per-field error message and moves focus to the first invalid field; the modal body has a visible scroll affordance.

title: Services chips look tappable but are decorative and hidden from assistive tech
element: Seven category pills (Become a property manager, Maintenance, Food & Essentials, Supplies, Transportation…)
evidence: live snapshot → `list [aria-hidden]` containing `listitem` text only, no buttons or links; `marketing__services__d1440.jpg` shows pill-shaped chips with icons and hover-ready styling
what: The page's only content block looks exactly like a set of filter buttons, is not interactive, and is explicitly removed from the accessibility tree.
why: Pointer users tap and nothing happens; screen-reader users are told the page has nothing beyond "Coming Soon". The chips also mix host services (property manager, agent, market properties) with guest services (food, supplies, transport) in one undifferentiated row.
fix: Either make them real links/buttons with destinations, or render them as plain text tags without pill affordance. Split host vs guest services and remove `aria-hidden`.
acceptance: Every chip is either a working link or a non-interactive label with no button affordance; content is exposed to assistive tech.

title: Legal pages have no table of contents or anchors
evidence: `marketing__terms__d1440.jpg`; live on /terms: 21 `<h2>` sections, 5,862px tall, **0** in-page `#` links, 16px/26px text at a 768px measure
what: Terms is a single 21-section column with no way to jump to "Cancellation", "Security deposits" or "AI features". The "last updated 9 November 2026" line is buried in the third sentence of the first section.
why: When someone actually needs a legal page it is because of a specific dispute, so they need one section fast. Without a ToC they scroll 5,800px or use browser find.
fix: Add a sticky section index (or a two-column layout with a ToC sidebar at ≥1024) built from the existing `h2`s with `id`s; surface "Last updated" as a meta line under the page title.
acceptance: Every legal page exposes a linked section index; the updated date appears in the page header at every width.

title: Unknown routes return HTTP 200 (soft 404)
evidence: manifest `status: 200` for `/this-route-does-not-exist`; the SPA renders the "This page wandered off / ERROR 404" screen
what: The HTML document returns 200 for every path, so crawlers index 404 pages as valid content; the same applies to the currently-stale `/for-hosts/v4`.
why: Duplicate/false pages dilute indexing, and any mistyped marketing URL becomes a permanent soft 404 in search results. It also means monitoring cannot distinguish a broken deploy from a real page.
fix: Serve a real 404 status for unknown paths at the edge/host (Vercel rewrite to the SPA only for known route prefixes, or a 404 function), keeping the styled screen.
acceptance: `curl -I http://<host>/this-route-does-not-exist` returns 404 while rendering the same page.

title: The login page's product tour auto-advances next to the email field
evidence: live: slide caption read "Intro", then "Bookings" after 5s with no interaction; pause/next controls exist
what: A full-bleed panel beside the login form changes image and caption every few seconds. It pauses only if the user finds the small pause button.
why: Motion adjacent to a text field competes for attention exactly when the user is typing an email, and it makes a two-field form feel busy. Automated motion is a WCAG 2.2.2 concern even when a pause control exists.
fix: Do not autoplay beside the form. Start paused on slide 1 with visible "Play tour" control, or respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and start paused for those users.
acceptance: The panel is static on load; no slide change occurs without a user action.

title: Login email validation is not programmatically announced
evidence: `host-login-empty.png` shows the inline red "Enter a valid email address"; live after submit → `input[aria-invalid] === null`, `[role=status]` text is empty
what: The error is visible but not linked to the field (`aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid` absent) and not announced through a live region.
why: Screen-reader users press Continue and get no feedback at all; they cannot tell why nothing happened.
fix: Set `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` to the error id, and render the error in an `aria-live="polite"` region that already exists in the DOM.

title: The guest form pre-fills a different fake person on every load
